title: Minor superficial burn on Bonfire Night
setting: Bonfire Night celebration. An 8-year-old child is brought to the post. Accidentally touched his cheek with the hot end of a used sparkler. Red skin, in pain.
verdictExplanation: Alert, responsive, stable observations. A minor, superficial dry burn on the cheek with no airway compromise. Not sick: simple burn management.

shared.danger: Crowds and active sparklers in the area
shared.airway: Open and clear, no soot or throat swelling
shared.circulation: Red skin and swelling along the cheek

history.history: Distracted by fireworks, touched cheek with hot end of a sparkler 5 minutes ago
history.injuries: Superficial burn to the right cheek
history.additional: Parents are present and highly concerned about scarring

followUp.question: What is the correct first aid management for this minor burn?

options.text: Cool the burn under clean, cool running water for 20 minutes, then cover with a clean dressing (e.g. cling film)
Apply butter, toothpaste, or burn cream immediately to soothe the skin
Burst any blisters that form and scrub the wound to keep it clean
Call 999 immediately for a critical paediatric emergency

followUp.explanation: All burns must be cooled under clean, cool running water for a full 20 minutes. Cover with cling film or a sterile non-adherent dressing. Never apply butter, toothpaste, or fats (they trap heat). Never burst blisters. 999 is not indicated for stable, minor superficial burns.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Cool the cheek with water/wet compress for 20 minutes. Reassure child and parents.
levelFlags.erNotes: Cool the burn for 20 minutes. Assess depth (superficial erythema). Cover loosely with non-adherent dressing or cling film. Advise onward medical review if scarring is a concern.
